data.title: Businesses urge faster action on electrification as COP31 enters final hours
data.description:
Key points:
  • More than 120 signatories to business statement
  • Intervention comes as draft text waters down language
  • Firms call for strong political signal in final deal

By Simon Jessop

More than 120 companies, investors and business groups including German engineering company Siemens and French lender BNP Paribas staged a late intervention at the COP31 climate talks on Thursday, urging an ambitious deal to accelerate electrification of the world economy.

The 123 signatories to the business statement followed the publication of a draft text that kept a goal of raising electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, but weakened the obligation on individual countries to act.

While some countries want the text to make explicit the need to generate that electricity from renewable sources, others are happy to be less specific, which could mean much of it would come from dirtier power sources like coal, activists said.

With the talks scheduled to end on Friday, the signatories said the final deal needed to secure strong language on backing rapid electrification to send a clear political signal that would encourage the clean energy investment needed across sectors.

"Electrification is an economic priority, and business needs certainty to invest," said Andrew Prag, managing director for policy at the We Mean Business Coalition, which organised the statement.

"COP31 must deliver the strongest possible signal to accelerate electrification."

Other signatories include Australian miner Fortescue , Dutch lender ING and Swiss consumer goods company Nestle , alongside investor and industry groups such as the Principles for Responsible Investment.

Faster electrification would help the world meet other goals agreed at previous COPs, including a push to triple renewable energy capacity, double the rate of improvements in energy efficiency and transition away from fossil fuels.

"Electrification is reshaping the global economy and the economics are compelling," We Mean Business CEO María Mendiluce said, citing energy costs, efficiency and reduced exposure to volatile fossil fuel markets.

data.title: Bending Spoons has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Mailchimp
data.description:
Bending Spoons S.p.A. has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Mailchimp, the email marketing automation platform for businesses, from Intuit, the global financial technology platform, at an enterprise value of $3.68 billion. In connection with the all-cash transaction, Intuit will invest $368 million of its proceeds into newly issued Bending Spoons equity. The acquisition, including the investment, is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.

“Mailchimp is a powerful brand, built over two decades of reshaping the email marketing category and redefining how companies grow their audiences,” said Luca Ferrari, Bending Spoons CEO and co-founder. “We’re honored to welcome it to Bending Spoons and excited about what we can accomplish together. After closing, we’ll invest substantially in the business, building on the powerful, easy-to-use tools customers already value and rely on.”

“Mailchimp has helped millions of businesses grow and acquire customers through email marketing automation, and we are grateful to the Mailchimp team for what they have built and the impact they have had on customers and Intuit,” said Jack Tam, Senior Vice President, Intuit. “We are confident Bending Spoons will lead Mailchimp to continued success in this next chapter. We are focused on ensuring a smooth transition for Mailchimp’s customers, partners, and employees.”

Details of the Proposed Transaction

Under the terms of the agreement, which was unanimously approved by the board of directors of Bending Spoons, Bending Spoons will acquire the Mailchimp business by purchasing 100% of The Rocket Science Group, LLC and other assets and liabilities of the Mailchimp business.

The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

Legal Counsel and Financial Advisors

Citi and J.P. Morgan are acting as co-lead financial advisors to Bending Spoons, and Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, Succursale Italia and UniCredit are acting as financial advisors on the transaction. Freshfields US LLP is serving as legal counsel to Bending Spoons, EY-Parthenon is providing financial due diligence services and EY STP tax due diligence services, and NewTeam is providing financial services.

About Bending Spoons

Bending Spoons is built on the conviction that operational excellence enables efficient growth through acquisitions. It acquires digital businesses, implements deep transformations and ongoing optimizations to sustainably expand earnings, and reinvests in additional acquisitions, thereby continuing the compounding cycle. The company has executed this strategy for more than a decade and, to date, has never sold a material business.

Bending Spoons strives to envision the most successful version of an acquired business, and works to close the gap between its current state and that vision as quickly and completely as possible. The transformation is typically deep and entails reorganizing teams, overhauling technology, redesigning user interfaces, accelerating product development, and enhancing marketing and monetization. AI is often both a central component of the vision and a key tool in implementing the transformation.

Bending Spoons’ performance is driven by its Platform—comprising its people, proprietary technologies, and proprietary data—and reflects an intense focus on achieving exceptional talent density, cultural strength, and technical capabilities.

Bending Spoons’ main businesses include Airtable, AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Miro, Tractive, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

data.title: Bending Spoons Announces Q3 2026 Results
data.description:
Bending Spoons S.p.A. () today announced its results for Q3 2026.

Highlights from Q3 2026:

  • Revenue was $780 million, up 125% from Q3 2025.

  • Operating income was $172 million, up 34% from Q3 2025. Adjusted Operating Income1 was $424 million, up 130% from Q3 2025.

  • Diluted earnings per share was $0.13, down 3% from Q3 2025. Adjusted Earnings per Share2 was $0.42, up 98% from Q3 2025.

  • We completed the acquisition of Airtable for an enterprise value of $1.29 billion. Airtable is a collaborative platform where organizations build and run workflows and applications.

  • At the end of the quarter, net debt was $4.00 billion and leverage ratio3 was 2.1×. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $1.02 billion, and we had $2.33 billion of available borrowing capacity under our undrawn committed term loan and revolving credit facilities.

Key events that occurred subsequent to the end of Q3 2026:

  • We entered into an agreement to acquire Mailchimp from Intuit for an enterprise value of $3.68 billion. Mailchimp helps millions of businesses plan, execute, and optimize their email marketing campaigns.

  • We completed the acquisition of Miro for an enterprise value of $1.36 billion. Miro supports teams as they brainstorm, plan, and execute projects together.

  • We raised $330 million of gross proceeds through a private placement with Berkshire Hathaway of 10 million ordinary shares of Bending Spoons.

  • We agreed to sell 32.5 million ordinary shares to new and existing investors in a private placement for expected gross proceeds of $1.30 billion.

  • We issued dual-currency senior secured notes comprising $1.25 billion of U.S. dollar-denominated notes and €500 million of euro-denominated notes, both issued at par and maturing in 2032.

  • We signed and drew a $1.25 billion add-on to our existing U.S. dollar-denominated term loan B and a €395 million add-on to our existing euro-denominated term loan B, both maturing in 2031.

Operating results (unaudited)

Revenue grew by $434 million, or 125%, from Q3 2025 to Q3 2026, primarily driven by acquisitions. The businesses acquired from the start of Q3 2025 until the end of Q3 2026 are Airtable, AOL, Eventbrite, Harvest, MileIQ, Tractive, and Vimeo. Organic revenue growth4 was 3% in Q3 2026, with Tractive and WeTransfer making the largest contributions. Growth in these businesses was partly offset by a decline in Remini revenue. Airtable contributed $38 million to Q3 revenue.

Gross profit grew by $181 million, or 78%, from Q3 2025 to Q3 2026, as cost of revenue increased by $252 million, or 221%. The increase in cost of revenue was primarily driven by the following:

  • An increase in amortization of acquired intangible assets, reflecting businesses acquired over the past year and the finalization of purchase price allocations for AOL, Eventbrite, Tractive, and Vimeo, which resulted in a $65 million catch-up charge relating to prior periods

  • An increase in IT infrastructure expense, reflecting an increase in cloud infrastructure utilization primarily driven by acquisitions

  • An increase in hardware-related costs, reflecting Tractive device sales

In Q3 2026, cost of revenue included the following items, which were adjusted in the calculation of our non-GAAP financial measures:

  • $189 million of amortization of acquired intangible assets

  • $1 million of reorganization-related expense

Operating income grew by $43 million, or 34%, from Q3 2025 to Q3 2026, resulting from the $181 million increase in gross profit noted above, partially offset by a $138 million increase in operating expenses. The increase in operating expenses primarily reflects personnel costs associated with the ongoing operation of newly acquired businesses, and separation packages offered to team members in connection with the reorganizations of Airtable, AOL, Tractive, and Vimeo.

In Q3 2026, operating expenses included the following items, which were adjusted in the calculation of our non-GAAP financial measures:

  • $24 million of reorganization-related expense

  • $19 million of transaction-related expense

  • $19 million of other items not considered indicative of core or ongoing operating performance

Net income grew by $6 million, or 7%, resulting from the $43 million increase in operating income noted above, and the net impact of the following:

  • A $67 million increase in interest expense, primarily driven by higher borrowings associated with acquisition financing

  • A $15 million increase in other expense (income), primarily driven by unfavorable changes in currency exchange rates

  • A $43 million increase in income tax benefit, primarily driven by the partial release of a valuation allowance in connection with the Vimeo acquisition, and the remeasurement of equity compensation obligations at our subsidiaries

In Q3 2026, other expense (income) included the following items, which were adjusted in the calculation of our non-GAAP financial measures:

  • $28 million of foreign exchange losses on assets and liabilities denominated in a non-functional currency

  • $1 million of gains from changes in the fair value of interest rate swaps

In Q3 2026, income tax expense (benefit) included a $57 million benefit arising from the partial release of a valuation allowance in connection with the finalized purchase price allocation for Vimeo. This item was adjusted in the calculation of our non-GAAP financial measures.

Diluted earnings per share decreased by 3%, resulting from the 7% increase in net income, more than offset by a 10% increase in diluted weighted-average shares outstanding.

Financial condition (unaudited)

At the end of Q3 2026, net debt totaled $4.00 billion, and leverage ratio was 2.1×.

Net debt comprised a long-term debt carrying amount of $4.91 billion, plus $118 million of unamortized issuance costs, less cash and cash equivalents of $1.02 billion. During the quarter, net debt decreased by $187 million, primarily reflecting the $1.09 billion aggregate net proceeds from our initial public offering and $261 million of net cash from operating activities, partially offset by $1.21 billion of net cash paid for acquisitions.

Available liquidity totaled $3.36 billion, comprising $1.02 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $1.74 billion available under our revolving credit facilities, and $0.60 billion of committed but undrawn term loan facilities.

Other highlights

On September 4, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Airtable for an enterprise value of $1.29 billion. Airtable is a collaborative platform where organizations build and run workflows and applications.

On September 10, 2026, we announced we had entered into an agreement to acquire Miro for an enterprise value of $1.36 billion. The acquisition closed on October 26, 2026. Miro supports teams as they brainstorm, plan, and execute projects together.

During Q3 2026, we continued improving our proprietary AI harness. It is built on open-source components and automatically selects the appropriate AI model for each task, balancing effectiveness and cost. Available models include a range of self-hosted, open-weight models, which we use for most tasks. For the most complex or highest-stakes tasks—and to supervise less advanced models—we use more expensive, closed-weight models. Our model-agnostic harness keeps us independent of any single third-party vendor.

Since the beginning of 2026, we have increased the number of pull requests5 per Spooner software engineer more than fourfold while reducing inference cost per pull request by roughly half, and by over 90% from mid-year peak levels. We see potential for further productivity gains as we continue to improve our capabilities in AI.

[Please see chart in the PDF version of this release on the company website]

We introduced Diagram, a proprietary AI-powered design tool. Specifically tailored to our workflows, we consider it superior to the third-party tools we were previously using for product design, preparation of slide decks, and other design tasks.

Leveraging proprietary technologies and improved processes, we significantly compressed our recruiting time for a few roles without any observed compromise in quality. This should allow us to improve our competitiveness in the acquisition of talent.

We commenced recruitment activities in the United States as part of our plan to broaden our presence in the country.

Highlights of our progress with recent acquisitions:

  • AOL. We substantially completed subscription pricing and packaging adjustments, migrated AOL’s desktop properties to a new instance of the advertising technology stack, rolled out the new desktop email client to all users, and undertook extensive testing across advertising and user experience, with several experiments showing measurable increases in engagement and advertising yield.

  • Eventbrite. We shipped approximately 30 product improvements during Q3, enhanced event discoverability by integrating with ChatGPT, introduced post-checkout advertising while further improving first-party advertising revenue, started piloting new subscription offerings for consumers and organizers, and reduced cloud infrastructure spend while simultaneously investing in capabilities that will improve technical robustness.

  • Tractive. We completed the reorganization, migrated the business onto our proprietary technologies, reduced customer service backlog by 80% by leveraging automated workflows, introduced automatic walk detection, scratching alerts, and better health insights, launched Dog 6 XL Adventure for larger dogs, expanded distribution by signing five new insurance partners and a leading European supermarket chain, and reduced annualized marketing spend by over $10 million through the elimination of unprofitable campaigns.

  • Vimeo. We continued to modernize the Vimeo experience and expand personalization options. We redesigned the OTT checkout flow, delivering an 11% increase in conversion to subscriptions in early testing, and embedded AI analytics in the enterprise offering. Median video transcoding time fell by 40% from the start to the end of Q3. Together with actions taken earlier in the year, the changes implemented in Q3 are expected to avoid more than $7 million of annual hosting costs.

More generally, we continued to improve the competitiveness of our businesses via product innovation. For example, we launched Brightcove Gen 2, which brings together a redesigned web video player, AI-generated live captions and universal translation, and AI-enabled agentic capabilities. At komoot, we introduced live tracking, which better positions the service to be used by running and cycling event organizers. At WeTransfer, we introduced end-to-end encrypted transfers for business customers, further strengthening the product as an enterprise-grade solution.

Outlook

For Q4 2026, we forecast the following results:

  • Revenue of $984 million to $1,000 million, implying year-over-year organic growth of 5% at the midpoint

  • Adjusted Operating Income of $470 million to $490 million6

For the full year 2026, we forecast the following results:

  • Revenue of $3.07 billion to $3.09 billion, implying year-over-year organic growth of 4% at the midpoint

  • Adjusted Operating Income of $1.58 billion to $1.60 billion6

These revised full year 2026 forecasts represent an increase from the previously provided $2.78 billion to $2.82 billion and $1.46 billion to $1.51 billion revenue and Adjusted Operating Income guidance ranges. Both increases reflect a stronger outlook for businesses included in our prior guidance and contributions from Airtable and Miro.

This outlook is based solely on the portfolio of businesses owned as of November 19, 2026, and does not include any contribution from additional acquisitions. Specifically, it includes a full quarter contribution from Airtable and Miro’s contribution from October 26, but no contribution from the pending Mailchimp acquisition.

Webcast and conference call

We will host a conference call to discuss our results at 8:00 a.m. ET (2:00 p.m. CET) on November 20, 2026. The live webcast of the call, along with this press release, will be available on our investor relations website at investors.bendingspoons.com. Following the call, a replay will be available on the same website.

We publish important information on our investor relations website, and may use it from time to time as a means of disclosing information to the market, potentially including material non-public information. Accordingly, investors should monitor our investor relations website, in addition to our press releases, filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, public conference calls, and webcasts.

About Bending Spoons

Bending Spoons is built on the conviction that operational excellence enables efficient growth through acquisitions. We acquire digital businesses, implement deep transformations and ongoing optimizations to sustainably expand earnings, and reinvest in additional acquisitions, thereby continuing the compounding cycle. We have executed this strategy for more than a decade and, to date, have never sold a material business.

We strive to envision the most successful version of an acquired business, and work to close the gap between its current state and that vision as quickly and completely as possible. The transformation is typically deep and entails reorganizing teams, overhauling technology, redesigning user interfaces, accelerating product development, and enhancing marketing and monetization. AI is often both a central component of our vision for the acquired business and a key tool in implementing the transformation.

Our performance is driven by our Platform—comprising our people, proprietary technologies, and proprietary data—and reflects our intense focus on achieving exceptional talent density, cultural strength, and technical capabilities.

Bending Spoons' main businesses include Airtable, AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Miro, Tractive, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

data.title: BayCom Corp Announces Cash Dividend
data.description:
BayCom Corp () (“BayCom” or the “Company”), the parent company of United Business Bank, today announced that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.30 per share on the Company's common stock. The dividend is payable on January 7, 2027, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on December 10, 2026.

About BayCom Corp

The Company, through its wholly owned operating subsidiary, United Business Bank, offers a full range of loans, including SBA, CalCAP, FSA and USDA guaranteed loans, and deposit products and services to businesses and their affiliates in California, Nevada, Washington, New Mexico and Colorado. The Bank is an Equal Housing Lender and a member of FDIC. The Company’s common stock is traded on the NASDAQ under the symbol “BCML”. For more information, go to www.unitedbusinessbank.com.

Forward-Looking Statements

Certain statements in this press release may constitute "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements relate to the Company's financial condition, results of operations, plans, objectives, future performance or business, including information regarding the ability of BayCom to pay dividends in the future. You should not place undue reliance on these statements, as they are subject to risks and uncertainties, and actual results and performance in future periods may be materially different from any future results or performance suggested by the forward-looking statements in this release. Factors that might cause such differences include, but are not limited to, the Company’s financial condition and results of operations, general economic conditions, as well as those within the Company’s industry, and numerous other factors identified in BayCom's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and other documents filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission. Such forward-looking statements speak only as of the date of this release. The Company expressly disclaims any obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements made herein to reflect any changes in the Company's expectations of results or any change in events.

US stocks slumped on Thursday, after Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revitalize faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its share price ebbed.

All three major US stock indexes ended the session sharply lower, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its fifth straight session of losses.

The S&P 500 was on course to post its steepest weekly loss since April 2025.

Anthropic's debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced late Wednesday at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. The stock opened at $111.50 shortly before noon. After the company's market valuation briefly surpassed $2 trillion, its momentum began to lose steam.

"The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri. "That money is coming from somewhere; investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from today's trading behavior, whether it's up or down."

Even so, Ellerbroek's enthusiasm for the AI trade has waned.

"My beliefs about the growth in data center capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two," he added. "Nvidia's crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact."

"Data centers are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly."

Advanced Micro Devices shares tumbled after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.

Most chipmakers were lower, including Micron and Broadcom , among others.

Nvidia marked its sixth straight session of losses after the chipmaker's upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed lower.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius sustained steep losses.

In other stocks, Palo Alto Networks shares jumped after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue guidance.

Walmart dipped after the retail giant's annual sales forecast disappointed investors.

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 148.39 points, or 2.03%, to end at 7,175.24 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 544.00 points, or 2.23%, to 23,885.88. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,102.71 points, or 2.20%, to 49,095.46.

FOCUS TURNS TO THE FED

Following Wednesday's release of minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting, investors are recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

The minutes revealed a desire to rein in inflation even prior to the recent release of consumer and producer price indexes, which showed price pressures heating up.

Financial markets are currently pricing in about a 94% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the central bank's December meeting, with a small but growing chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Next week, the Commerce Department is expected to release its personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, which includes the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index. Analysts expect the report to show year-on-year core inflation of 3.2%, well above the central bank's 2% annual target.

data.title: UniFirst, Cintas executives to meet with FTC on Friday - CTFN
data.description:
UniFirst CEO Steven Sintros and Cintas CEO Todd Schneider are expected to have a meeting with the Federal Trade Commission on Friday.

It's not clear what will be discussed at the meeting and whether it's a “last rites” meeting, according to a CTFN report on Thursday, which cited unidentified sources. On Monday, there was a meeting between UniFirst and Cintas lawyers and outside counsel to prepare for the Friday meeting.

Semafor on Friday reported that the FTC will soon have a “last rites” meeting with the parties. These meetings between the antitrust regulator and the parties are typically a precursor to a formal lawsuit.

The latest update comes after a Semafor report late Wednesday that Cintas () Chairman Scott Farmer met with President Donald Trump recently to try to salvage its $5.5 billion purchase of rival UniFirst (), as the FTC may sue to block the combination. Farmer met with Trump to try to have him intervene, as FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson appears inclined to challenge the deal.

The president has signaled that he will defer to Ferguson's judgment, one person familiar told Semafor. A CTFN story on Friday implied that Washington, D.C. lobbyists for Cintas and UniFirst may not be able to get the deal over the goal line.

Cintas has engaged legal counsel and expects the FTC to file a lawsuit, according to the Semafor report. Cintas has indicated to some investors that it may seek a divestiture package to try to thwart a lawsuit, though internally the company doesn't appear to want to divest.

The UniFirst/Cintas deal spread widened to $93 on Thursday from $85 on Wednesday. The spread narrowed on Wednesday after a report indicated that the companies were cautiously optimistic that the FTC would clear the combination unconditionally and were planning for integration.

Cintas () agreed to acquire smaller rival UniFirst ( for $310 per share in cash and stock in March, representing an enterprise value of about $5.5B.

data.title: Plunging oil refining margins signal inflation relief for central banks
data.description:
Global oil refining margins are collapsing back toward pre-war levels, giving central banks and bond-market investors a far clearer sign of cooling inflation than falling crude prices alone, according to Javier Blas, an energy and commodities columnist at Bloomberg.

Benchmark 3-2-1 crack spreads—which measure the theoretical profit from turning three barrels of crude into two barrels of gasoline and one barrel of diesel—have tumbled to between $25 and $40 a barrel from peaks of $60 to $75 just weeks ago, Blas noted in a social media post.

The steepest retreat has hit Asia, where Dubai-linked margins have plunged to near $20 a barrel from above $60 a barrel in October, approaching their early-2026 baseline before Middle East conflict disrupted global processing capacity. European margins tied to Brent crude have fallen over the same stretch to roughly $28 a barrel from nearly $60, while U.S. WTI margins have slipped to under $40 from highs near $70.

A sharp slide in wholesale gasoline prices has driven much of the contraction, Blas wrote, as seasonal demand slows and steady refinery output keeps fuel supplies abundant.

For monetary policymakers and fixed-income markets, narrowing refining margins carry more weight than headline crude futures because households and freight operators buy finished fuels rather than raw oil. After months in which processing bottlenecks kept pump and diesel prices elevated, the ongoing normalization in spreads removes a stubborn upside risk to consumer price growth.

data.title: Jacob Coxon Joins Protesters Outside Anthropic's HQ — WSJ
data.description:
By Erin Woo

Over 100 protestors, including prominent AI-safety activists and "swarm chasers," gathered outside Anthropic's San Francisco headquarters, chanting and waving signs reading "Stop the AI Race" and "Don't Build AI That Builds AI."

Their complaint: Anthropic bills itself as the most safety-conscious artificial-intelligence developer but is at the same time leading what critics say is a headlong race toward so-called recursive self-improvement, sometimes called RSI, meaning AI that can improve itself.

The protest was organized by a group calling itself Ban RSI, whose website reads: "Anthropic uses AI to build better AI. They are making trillions doing so."

Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic researcher whose resignation spurred a wave of AI fears this fall, made an appearance. He called for Anthropic to lobby the government for better regulation, work with the other AI companies to coordinate on safety, and unilaterally slow down AI progress if other options fail.

"We're here because this technology is threatening our lives," Coxon said.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Fed's Barr worried regulatory changes may increase financial sector risks
data.description:
By Michael S. Derby

Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said on Thursday that US financial regulation changes underway at the central bank could make it harder to identify and respond to future market troubles.

Barr had been the Fed's top financial supervision official until early 2025, at the beginning of President Donald Trump's second term, when he gave up the role in what he said was an effort to preserve Fed independence.

His successor, Michelle Bowman, has pursued a deregulation effort that aims to increase accountability, but which has raised concerns about gaps in oversight.

“I'm not worried about it in a today sense,” but these changes “are things that have longer term tails to them, longer term consequences, and so there can be a gradual weakening over time in supervision” that makes the banking system less safe, Barr said at the FinRegLab 2026 AI Symposium.

Barr said that around a third of Fed bank regulator jobs in Washington are on the chopping block, adding that, during the 2007-2009 global financial crisis, the central bank lacked sufficient talent on its staff that could quickly identify and understand problems.

Those changes alongside others “add up," he said. "Not any one of them is ... a risk tomorrow, but ... I think there are risks worth worrying about.”

Barr added that he has been "very public" about his disagreements with "the direction of travel" in Fed supervision and regulation over the last year and a half.

Turning to monetary policy, Barr repeated that he believes the Fed will need to raise interest rates again. “Inflation is too high,” he said, “so I think we're going to need to adjust monetary policy further.”

The Fed next meets on December 8 and 9, when it is expected to increase its current 3.75% to 4% interest rate target range by a quarter percentage point. It is expected to hike again in the new year as it works to lower price pressures.
